property_summary: Executing a scheduled operation before its computed ready time must revert and leave the operation still scheduled and not done.
After a successful schedule, cancel removes the pending operation (timestamp becomes 0) for any proposer-controlled operation.
After a successful call to grantRole(role, account) on a default-admin role, hasRole(role, account) is true.

For any non-default role whose admin is the DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE, granting that role to any address makes hasRole(role, account) true, provided the caller holds the DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE and the account does not already have the role.
Granting a role from its admin succeeds and makes hasRole(role, account) true.

For any role whose admin role is itself, a freshly deployed C grants that role only to the contract itself; no external account can hold a self-administered role unless the contract explicitly grants it, so grantRole and renounceRole for such roles cannot make an arbitrary external account a member.

property_summary: For any account and any role, the role membership observed by hasRole after the test performs a grantRole followed by a revokeRole can differ from the initial membership only if the caller has the role's admin role; for accounts without that admin role, the grant and revoke calls revert and the membership stays exactly as it was.
For any role and account where the caller lacks the role's admin role, grantRole and revokeRole both revert and leave hasRole unchanged.

For any role whose admin role is a non-zero role that the caller does not hold, calling grantRole on a fresh C reverts and does not change whether the target account has that role, and getRoleAdmin remains unchanged.

For any role whose admin role is a non-zero role that the caller does not hold, calling grantRole on a fresh C reverts and does not change whether the target account has that role, and getRoleAdmin remains unchanged.
A successfully executed operation (one whose hash was previously scheduled and is ready) is marked done, so getTimestamp returns _DONE_TIMESTAMP (1) immediately after execution.
After a newly granted access-control role R is revoked from an account, hasRole(R, account) returns false.
Executing a scheduled operation before its delay has elapsed must revert, leaving getTimestamp greater than 1 (still pending) rather than done.
An operation scheduled with delay greater than the minimum delay reverts when executed before its delay has elapsed, leaving it pending (timestamp > 1) and unchanged.
Executing a scheduled operation before its delay elapses reverts and leaves its timestamp greater than the done sentinel (1).
getMinDelay() always returns the initial minimum delay because no external call can change it (updateDelay is self-call only).
getMinDelay() returns the initial minimum delay unchanged after any role-granting call, because no call originating from the test contract can self-invoke updateDelay.
updateDelay is self-call only, so any externally invoked call leaves getMinDelay unchanged.
updateDelay always reverts when called by an account other than the timelock contract itself, leaving the minimum delay unchanged.
Any externally attempted updateDelay call reverts and leaves getMinDelay() unchanged.
For any caller with PROPOSER_ROLE, scheduling a new operation with delay exactly getMinDelay makes it pending at block.timestamp + getMinDelay and not ready immediately.
For any operation scheduled with a delay greater than or equal to the current minimum delay, its stored timestamp equals block.timestamp + delay, and it is pending but not ready.
